title: F.P.Journe Octa Lune Ref. LN Boutique Edition 40mm in 18k RG Full Set Unpolished
description: The moonphase on these watches is spectacular and incredibly attractive. The example is 40mm in diameter. The case is unpolished. The watch is powered by the calibre 1300.3 with retrograde power reserve indication of 120 hours. Complicated F.P.Journe models have been achieving records at auction in recent months. A platinum Resonance example just sold for $762,000 and a pink gold Resonance example just sold for $685,800 . The interest in F.P.Journe has skyrocketed and these are incredibly special timepieces. This watch comes from the original owner who purchased it in 2024 and is one of the last ones produced. It comes full set with the original box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It comes with the original F.P.Journe leather strap. It is paired on a Jean Rousseau leather strap.

title: Joe DiMaggio's Patek Philippe Breguet Dial Reference 130 Chronograph in 18K YG w/ Extract
description: This remains the longest consecutive-game hitting streak in MLB history to this day! Throughout the May 15 to July 16, 1941 streak, he batted .408 with 15 home runs and 55 RBIs. Joltin’ Joe’s career started alongside the “Iron Horse” Lou Gehrig and ended alongside Micky Mantle. He operated at the intersection of two legendary Yankees eras (with Gehrig who played alongside Babe Ruth and was part of the Murderers’ Row 1927 Yankees team) and then with Mantle who of course had the legendary home run duel with his teammate Roger Maris in 1961. From 1943–1945, DiMaggio served in the U.S. Army Air Forces during World War II (which many cite as his prime years). DiMaggio had a lifetime batting average of .325 and accumulated 361 home runs. In 1955, DiMaggio was elected into the National Baseball Hall of Fame. In 1969, Joe DiMaggio was voted the greatest living baseball player. He famously married Marilyn Monroe in 1954 and they had a short marriage, but they rekindled their relationship years later and were reportedly close to marrying again before Monroe passed in 1962. According to the Extract from the Archives, this timepiece was produced in 1947 and was sold on December 12, 1948. The dial features beautiful hand-cut Breguet numerals which are confirmed in the Extract notes. It features the tachymeter scale demarcated for miles on the perimeter of the dial. This example features the spade hand configuration which was popular in the American market during the late 1940s. The watch is powered by the prestigious calibre 13-130 which was featured in many of the most important chronographs from Patek Philippe in this period. The case measures 33mm in diameter, and wears large at 41mm lug-to-lug. The 18k yellow gold case was produced by Emile Vichet, the Geneva master casemaker and features the Poinçon de Maître number 9. title: Cartier Tank Cintrée Ivory Dial WGTA0057 100th Anniversary in 18K YG Unpolished Full Set
description: This Cartier Tank Cintrée WGTA0057 is an incredibly special timepiece commemorating the 100th Anniversary of the iconic Cartier Tank Cintrée. The watch was introduced in 2021, and was among one of the most celebrated timepieces. This is a limited edition of only 150 examples. The 18k yellow gold case measures approximately 46mm by 23mm. The condition is outstanding and no signs of wear. It features the beautiful “Ivory” dial wth painted Roman numerals. The watch features blue Breguet hands. It is paired on the original Cartier leather strap and yellow gold buckle. For those interested in a sophisticated dress watch, this is an amazing choice. The watch comes with full set with box and papers. It is running well and keeping excellent time.

title: Patek Philippe 2nd Series Reference 3940P in Platinum w/ Extract Unpolished
description: The Patek Philippe reference 3940 perpetual calendar is one of the most elegant complicated timepieces one can find from any manufacturer. The Patek Philippe reference 3940 is one of the ultimate in discreet complications. The reference 3940 was introduced in 1985 and remained in production until circa 2007. Many collectors consider the reference 3940 and reference 3970 to be the most important complicated timepieces to be introduced in the 1980s. This watch features the thin self-winding calibre 240Q with microrotor. The case is 36mm and is made of platinum. The case appears to be unpolished with very strong hallmarks. The watch has a solid case back (which are exclusive for the platinum examples as they never featured exhibition case backs). The watch features the highly desired 2nd series dial with English calendar. It comes with a Patek Philippe black leather strap and platinum buckle. It does not come with box and papers. It does come with an Extract from the Archives. The watch was produced and sold in 1992. We do not know the service history, but it is running well and keeping good time.

title: Patek Philippe Nautilus 5980/60G-001 Flyback Chronograph in 18k WG Unpolished Full Set
description: This Patek Philippe Nautilus reference 5980/60G-001 is one of the most desirable Patek Philippe wristwatches. The Patek Philippe Nautilus reference 5980/60G-001 was introduced in April 2024. It is cherished by collectors for the sporty style and casual look. This watch is a fantastic Nautilus with flyback chronograph movement. The watch is powered by the automatic calibre CH 28-520 C. The 18k white gold case measures 40.5mm in diameter. The case is unpolished. It is comes with the original calfskin denim pattern strap and also comes wth the additional original fabric pattern, blue-gray. The watch is paired on the original 18k white gold deployant buckle. The watch was sold in 2026 and is in outstanding condition. The watch comes “full set” with box and the Certificate of Origin and pin pusher. The watch is running well and keeping great time.

title: Patek Philippe Tiffany & Co. Aquanaut 5167/1A-001 Full Set w/ Extra Strap
description: This Patek Philippe Aquanaut reference 5167/1A-001 is an incredibly special sports watch from the leading name in watchmaking. It is particularly important with the highly coveted double-signed dial from prestigious New York retailer Tiffany & Co. Tiffany-signed watches from Patek Philippe and Rolex are certainly the most desirable timepieces, so this Aquanaut reference 5167 is definitely a grail watch. The stainless steel case has been lightly polished. It measures 40mm in diameter. It is in fantastic condition. It is powered by the calibre 26-330 S C. This watch comes full set with box and Certificate of Origin. It was originally sold in 2015. We do not know the service history but it is running well. It comes with an additional Patek Philippe rubber strap.

title: Patek Philippe 24-Hour Display Travel Time 5224R-001 in 18K RG Full Set Unpolished
description: The Patek Philippe Travel Time reference 5224R-001 is a very special and interesting wristwatch. The watch was introduced in 2023. The watch features a stunning blue dial. It is powered by the in-house calibre 31-260 PS FUS 24H. The 18k rose gold case measures 42mm in diameter and 10.2mm in height. The watch is in outstanding condition and remains unpolished. It is paired on the original strap and 18k rose gold buckle. The watch is running well. It comes full set with box and papers. The watch was sold in 2025. This watch retails for $67,267

title: Patek Philippe Reference 3567/1 in 18K White Gold Unpolished w/ Extract
description: This Patek Philippe reference 3567/1 is a special time-only dress watch dating to 1971. The case is made by Ateliers Réunis S.A with the 28th key of Geneva. Ateliers Réunis S.A would be purchased by Patek Philippe in circa 1977 and would become one of the more common case makers seen in timepieces from the 1970s-1980s (most famously in the Nautilus reference 3700). This watch is a spectacular timepiece that features a beautiful integrated bracelet. The length will fit a wrist 7.2 inches. The dial and bracelet features a hammered texture which is very interesting. The dial features blue hour markers with exception to 1 o’clock. It is not clear whether these markers were born blue. The watch is powered by the manual wind calibre 175. The case measures 26mm by 32mm in length. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers. It comes with an Extract from the Archives.

title: Patek Philippe Breguet Dial Reference 5940J-001 in 18K YG Full Set Unpolished
description: The Patek Philippe reference 5940 perpetual calendar is one of the most elegant complicated timepieces one can find from any manufacturer. The 5940 was introduced in 2012 and this example was sold in December 2012 -a first year production. This particular example is in yellow gold. The dial is English with beautiful applied Breguet numerals. The dial is gorgeous and one of the most attractive dials from the era. These are also a fraction of the price of early 3940s. These feature the cushion case design that has become increasingly popular in recent years. It measures 37mm and 45mm lug to lug. The case appears to be unpolished. It features an exhibition case back. The watch features the iconic ultra-thin self-winding calibre 240Q with microrotor. The watch comes with an Certificate of Origin. It comes on an original Patek Philippe buckle in 18k yellow gold and box.

title: Patek Philippe Heures Sautantes Diamond Set Reference 3619/3 in 18K White Gold Unpolished w/ Extract
description: This is an incredibly special and possibly unique Patek Philippe referece 3619/3 in 18k white gold. The watch is fresh to market from the family of the original owner. The original owner purchased the watch from Patek Philippe in the 1970s and was a successful New York based attorney. It is massive case measuring 40mm in diameter by 35mm in length. The bracelet is an intricately woven white gold design that is extremely comfortable on the wrist. The watch will fit a wrist approximately 7.5 inches. These cases were produced by Ateliers Réunis. This particular example appears to be a specially requested example with the unseen diamond bezel. It features 50 brilliant diamonds throughout the bezel and 12 diamond hour markers on the dial. The dial features an indentation between 11 and 12 o’clock. The watch is powered by the “Heures Sautantes” (Jumping Hours) manual-wind calibre 27 HS 400. This imporant calibre also used in the iconic Patek Philippe Travel Time reference 2597. In 1959 this movement was introduced by Patek Philippe through the Swiss Patent 340,191 and was based on a 1953 prototype wristwatch from Louis Cottier. These case profile features two adjustments for setting the travel time forward or backward. The watch was found with the travel time set to the local time concealing the third hand. When the son of the original owner was informed of this important complication they were astonished. These timepieces are incredibly rare. It is estimated that 32 examples of the reference 3619 were made with only 13 examples sold publicly. Many were made with leather straps, and others with integrated bracelets. Dials often feature “ribbon” diamond hour markers for black dials and satiné blue dials will feature the more traditional single diamond hour markers. One example in white gold with white lacquered dial with Breguet numerals on leather strap sold in May of 2026 for approximately $447,000 . title: Patek Philippe Nautilus Reference 3711/1G in 18k White Gold w/ Box & Extract
description: The Patek Philippe Nautilus is perhaps the most desired watch on the planet. The introduction of the model marked the first true sports watch from the manufacturer in 1976. Along with the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, it ushered in the world of integrated stainless steel watches which are adored by watch enthusiasts today. This Patek Philippe Nautilus is a very special and rare reference 3711/1 in 18k white gold. It is believed 700 examples were produced. The 3711/1G was the successor reference to the 3700/1A. Lord David Snowdon famously wore one for years that was sold at Christie’s. The case is a “Jumbo” and measures 42mm in diameter. It has been lightly polished but is attractive. The reference 3711 was introduced in circa 2004 and was only produced until 2006. This is example dates to 2005. The watch is powered by the calibre 315 SC. It features a beautiful black dial. The 3711 is certainly one of the most attractive iterations of the Nautilus and this is an outstanding example. The watch comes with box. It comes with an Extract from the Archives. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Reference 2508 in 18K YG w/ Certificate of Origin

For those looking for an incredible mid-century Patek Philippe, this is a special watch. It is powered by the calibre 27 SC. This example was sold in the 1963. The non-luminous dial is extremely attractive. The 18K yellow gold case has been lightly polished in the past but is attractive and strong. It features a hallmark at 6 o’clock between the lugs. It is 35mm in diameter and produced by François Borgel (Taubert Frères). For those looking for an incredible mid-century Patek Philippe, this is a special watch. It comes from an important collector who Eric and Charlie admire. GREAT PROVENANCE. It is paired on a Patek Philippe leather strap and 18k yellow gold buckle. The watch comes with the Certificate of Origin. It does not come with a box. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Retailed by Brock & Co. Reference 42 Tank in 18K White Gold w/ Extract
description: This is an incredibly special rectangular timepiece from Patek Philippe dating to 1927. The watch is an early wristwatch produced in a time when the primary exports in Switzerland were pocket watches. The wristwatch would eventually become more prominent for Patek Philippe by the early 1930s. This example is a very rare model that was produced for the Beverly Hills based retailer Brock & Co. There are a handful of Patek Philippe wristwatches for Brock & Co of this era. Examples from this period include the references 42 and 425 made of gold or platinum. The designs of these watches were reminiscent of the trend-setting Cartier Tank. The Tank had been released about decade prior, and the Art Deco styles defined the watch industry throughout the 1920s. The dial features an incredible two-tone sector dial with the “Cat Whiskers” hour markers (2, 4, 8, and 9 o’clock). Both the manufactuer and retailer signature are engraved hard enamel. The case is made of 18k white gold. It measures approximately 33mm in length by 25mm in diameter. It has been lightly polished. The case design is quite incredible, as it is reminiscent of the pocket watches and features a hinged case at 12 o’clock. The watch is powered by the manual wind calibre 9 movement with lever escapement. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers. The watch comes with an Extract from the Archives.

title: The Baden Baden Jewelry Collection Including Jewelry worn on the Drake 'Take Care' Album
description: The Baden Baden Jewelry Collection Including Jewelry worn on the Drake 'Take Care' Album Wind Vintage is pleased to present the Baden Baden jewelry collection, an archive of custom jewelry and design history that includes pieces worn by Drake for the artwork of his landmark 2011 album, Take Care. Released in 2011, ‘Take Care’ is regarded by many Drake fans as his best album, and it is widely considered one of the most important and influential albums of the 2010s. It is a Certified Diamond album by the RIAA selling over 10 million copies (a record achieved by approximately 100 albums in history). The album spent 400 weeks on the Billboard 200 chart, is ranked 95th on Rolling Stone’s 500 Greatest Albums of All Time , and won Best Rap album of the 55th Grammy Awards (Drake’s first of five Grammys). Aubrey “Drake” Graham was photographed for the cover art and additional photographs by Hyghly Alleyne and Lamar Taylor wearing the associated collection of jewelry. This is an incredible opportunity to own Hip-hop jewelry worn by Drake on the album cover of ‘Take Care’. Additional photos of the jewelry can be seen here . The jewelry comes from the original owner who was a colleague of Drake during the breakthrough years of the musician’s career and formerly owned the Rolex GMT-Master II Ref 116758SANR worn on the album cover which we recently sold. Created between 2009 and 2011, the gold jewelry formed part of a larger collection made by Baden Baden for Drake. The pieces offered here have remained in the original owner’s archive since their manufacture. The large anchor chain and both bracelets were custom manufactured in Italy by Nicolis Cola for Baden Baden in 2011. The remaining jewelry was custom made in New York City, where all diamond setting was also completed. All diamonds are natural. title: Spencer Tracy's Rolex Explorer Reference 6350 w/ Waffle Dial Unpolished
description: This Rolex Explorer reference 6350 is an incredibly rare and important example from the early 1950s which belonged to American actor Spencer Tracy. This watch was worn in the 1956 movie ‘The Mountain’, an adventure film starring Spencer Tracy and Robert Wagner based on the French novel La neige en deuil. It is possibly one of the earliest product placements of a Rolex in a film. This example features an outstanding black “honeycomb” or “waffle” dial with very attractive lume. The textured Rolex dials of the 1950s are very uncommon and particularly important on Rolex sports models! It is paired on a Rolex Oyster Rivet bracelet with 64 end links dating to 1957 which we added and is period correct. The watch also comes with a Rolex strap and steel buckle which was worn on the Explorer for many years by Tracy. Linked here is a photo of Tracy wearing the watch. This example dates to circa 1953 with a 955,XXX serial It measures 36mm in diameter. The case appears to be unpolished. I’m often asked about which watches I would love to own if I could have anything. Watches like this waffle-dial Rolex Explorer 6350 is at the top of the list and the added provenance is an incredible bonus. This watch certainly belongs in the Rolex Museum collection - as it is the best of the best! To learn more about the history and evolution of the Rolex Explorer I, you can see my video and corresponding article Reference Points A Comprehensive Collector's Guide To The Rolex Explorer I . This watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Rolex Small Crown Submariner Reference 6536-1 Unpolished
description: The Rolex “Small Crown” Submariner reference 6536 is a classic reference and one of the iconic dive watches. I purchased this watch in 2020 from the sons of the original owner, Louis “Lou” Ross, who led a distinguished career of public service including as an aide to President Kennedy. Lou served as a Foreign Service Officer and wore this Submariner while posted around the world. When he retired, he put the watch away and his sons only recently found it after their mother passed. Amazingly, it seemed that the watch had not been opened since it left Rolex in 1957 and it remains all original including the crystal with slight crazing and original bracelet. Lou’s story is definitely worth telling in greater detail in the future, he was orphaned at age 3 and went on to record the Nuremberg trials as a very young man for the U.S. Government before embarking on a career of public service at important posts around the world, but given all the current interest in Submariners I felt it would be worth showing one of the great ones. The case measures 38mm in diameter (48mm lug-to-lug). The case appears to be unpolished. These models wear very nice on the wrist and are extremely this and light. It features the original “no hash” bezel which is original for pre-1957 and early 1957 Submariners. It was serviced for the first and only time in 2020. The luminous-hour markers have a warm patina which is much more beautiful in person. Complementing the warm lume is the awesome gilt font and chapter ring. The watch dates to circa 1957 and has a 230,XXX serial. It is paired on the original Rolex stretch Rivet bracelet dated to 1957. This watch should be in the Rolex Museum! To learn more about the Rolex Submariner, you can read my ‘ Reference Points: Understanding The Rolex Submariner ’ article and corresponding video. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Rolex FAP Peruvian Air Force Daytona Reference 6263
description: This Rolex Daytona reference 6263 is an awesome watch issued to the Peruvian Air Force. The Peruvian Air Force (Fuerza Aerea del Perú) ordered a small number of Daytonas in the 1970s and they say “FUERZA AEREA DEL PERÚ” (or FAP for short) around the edge. These are extremely interesting watches as we don’t often associate Daytonas with military use. This example features a 3.99M serial dating to circa 1975. The dial is very attractive. It features a replaced bezel, but has period Mark 2 pushers we found and placed on the watch. The central seconds hand is a replacement with a longer triangular tip, but is attractive. It is paired on an 78350 Oyster solid link bracelet with incorrect 557 end links, but they work well. The case has been lightly polished. It is powered by the manual-wind movement Caliber 727 made by Valjoux and is 37mm in diameter. The watch does not come with box or papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. This is a rare FAP Daytona and we are excited to be offering it for sale!

title: Rolex GMT-Master Reference 6542 Bakelite Bezel
description: The Rolex GMT-Master reference 6542 marked the first reference in what would go onto become one of the most celebrated timepieces across all manufacturers. The timepiece became an icon within the James Bond movie Goldfinger after being worn by Honor Blackman during her portrayal of "Pussy Galore". It is an unmistakable watch and it is seen as grail watches for collectors who understand the importance of the 1950s Rolex sports catalog. This particular example is an outstanding 6542 with a spectacular dial, vivid original Bakelite bezel, and great provenance. These Bakelite bezels have a propensity for cracks and are radioactive, and as a result many were replaced with non-luminous, anodized aluminum bezels. The colors are so unique and it makes for an out of this world aesthetic. In addition to the Bakelite bezel, the dial is very well preserved and attractive. The reference 6542 dials are often known for cracking and crazing, but this example has one of the nicest dial we have seen on any reference 6542. The GMT hand has minimal lume loss, but this is expected in a sports watch over 65 years old. The case has been lightly polished, but is very attractive and full. The watch has a 398,XXX serial dating to circa late 1958. It is 38mm in diameter (48mm lug-to-lug). It is paired on what is likely its original Swiss-made Oyster rivet bracelet with super-desirable “Big Logo” clasp and 65 end links dating to 1959. It has been in an important private collection for a number of years. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. The watch recently passed a water resistance test of 3 bar. To learn more about the Rolex GMT-Master, you can watch my ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Rolex GMT-Master' video and read the corresponding article. I selected this exact watch for inclusion in the Reference Points article and video, so that should tell you how I feel about the quality of this example.

This is an incredible Rolex GMT-Master 1675 with a rare double-signed dial from the Venezuelan retailer Serpico Y Laino and engraved case back. These double-signed gilt GMT-Masters are incredibly rare, and to feature one with the prestigious retailer of the finest Rolex and Patek Philippe models is truly special. It has a 1.14M serial number dating to circa 1964-1965. It features an incredible gilt dial. The luminous material is attractive. The aluminum bezel insert features a beautiful blue and autumn red color which is one of my favorites of all time. The case has been polished in the past. It is paired on a tight Rolex 7206 Rivet bracelet with 58 end links dating to 1964. It does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar. title: Rolex King Midas Ref 4315 in 18K Yellow Gold
description: The King Midas was the most expensive Rolex by far at retail in the 1960s and 1970s. The case is lightly polished, but in strong condition overall. The watch measures 40mm in diameter. It previously came from the original owner. The amazing tropical dial has the original tritium lume on the dial and hands. The aluminum bezel insert has faded to a beautiful grey color. The watch features a 1.7 million serial with inside case back dating to circa 1967. These were not assembled by Rolex to be Sea-Dwellers until later. The watch came from the original owner who purchased it new in New Zealand in the early 1970s. The gentleman’s wife was upset about the cost of the watch, but it was already purchased. The gentleman was a roofer and did various forms of manual labor. One day, he was on a roof and he took his watch off and left it on the roof so it would not get damaged while he was working. Unfortunately, he slipped and fell off the roof. He went to the hospital for a few days and when he regained his senses he realized his Rolex was probably still on the roof. He went back about a week later once he had left the hospital and promptly climbed onto the roof to find his watch still sitting there. He joked that spending the week in the sun up on the roof might have helped the dial turn “tropical” brown. The watch does not come with box and papers. Overall, this is an amazing opportunity to get a spectacular and rare Rolex sports watch. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. title: Tornek-Rayville by Blancpain Reference TR-900 Unpolished
description: The Tornek Rayville reference TR-900 by Blancpain is an iconic dive watch made for the U.S. Navy in the 1960s. These are incredibly rare and highly-coveted versions of the Fifty Fathoms with a great story. These watches were sold by Blancpain under the “Tornek-Rayville” name during the 1960s as a way to be supportive of the “Buy American Act “by way of Blancpain’s United States distributor Allen Tornek. They used the word “Rayville” as an English take on Blancpain’s associated history with the Swiss village Villeret. These watches were introduced in 1964, There were a purported 780 delivered to the United States in that first year. Another 300 examples were purportedly delivered in 1966 - this example coming from the later batch. In the 1970s, the U.S. government destroyed the majority of these watches. It is estimated that fewer than 100 examples still exist. This example is quite cool for anyone who has a penchant for the Rolex Explorer I as it features the case back serial 1016. The sandblasted stainless steel case measures 41mm in diameter. It has come to our attention that the springbars were later reapplied with the current fixed springbars. The hands have been relumed due to previous cracking / fissures. These watches feature the unique humidity indicator on the dials that would alert the wearer if humidity or water were to enter the watch. The watch is powered by the automatic A. Schild calibre 1361. The bezels of these watches are often susceptible to cracking. This example is intact and extremely attractive. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with box or papers, which is of course to be expected for a U.S.-military issued watch.

description: A Unpolished The Overseas line has recently seen a great deal of appreciation by collectors, and we are excited to offer this rare example that highlights the heritage of the iconic watch model. This Vacheron Constantin reference 42040/423A (42040-423A) is the younger sibling of the integrated sports model, reference 222. The dial is the rare salmon dial variant which is among the most desirable Overseas models. The stainless steel case measures approximately 36.5mm in diameter. These watches were introduced in the mid 1990s. We believe this example dates to the late 1990s - early 2000s. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Vacheron & Constantin Les Historiques Chronograph Ref. 47111/000J Full Set Unpolished
description: This Vacheron & Constantin Historiques Chronograph reference 47111/000J is a fantastic and modern chronograph. These are among the most interesting and well made VC chronographs. The watch is powered by the calibre 1141. The case is made of 18K yellow gold and appears to be unpolished. It measures 37mm in diameter and approximately 44mm lug-to-lug. For those looking for a sophisticated Vacheron & Constantin chronogaph, these are incredible watches. The watch comes full set with box and papers. It was sold in Japan in 2006. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Vacheron & Constantin Reference 6908 in 18k YG Unpolished
description: This Vacheron & Constantin reference 6908 is a spectacular timepiece with a bark-like textured case. The 18K yellow gold exterior is made by Wenger. The dimensions measure 26.5mm x 26.5mm. The bracelet should fit a wrist up to 6 inches. The buckle features a pronounced Maltese cross. The watch is powered by the manual wind calibre 1003. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well and keeping great time..

title: Vacheron Constantin Overseas Reference 42542/423A-8930 Mid-Size Unpolished
description: The Overseas line has recently seen a great deal of appreciation by collectors, and I am proud to offer this example that highlights the heritage of the iconic watch model. This Vacheron Constantin is the younger sibling of the integrated sports model, reference 222. It is the mid-size case. The watch features a white dial with diamond hour markers as well as a diamond set bezel. The stainless steel case measures 37mm in diameter (40mm including the crown). The watch fits a wrist approximately 7 inches. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch does not come with box or papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Concept Black Panther Flying Tourbillon Full Set
description: This Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Concept Black Panther is an amazing concept Audemars Piguet Flying Tourbillon. This model was released in 2021 through Audemars Piguet with their brand ambassadors Kevin Hart, Serena Williams, LeBron James, along with François-Henri Bennahmias. The initial watch was sold for charity on livestream for $5,200,000. This case is made of sandblasted titanium. It measures 42mm in diameter. It features a black ceramic bezel and crown, sapphire crystal and caseback. It is powered by the calibre 2965. It is a limited edition of 250 examples. The watch was sold in 2021. The watch comes full set with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak 15550SR.OO.1356SR.02 Full Set
description: The Audemars Piguet Royal Oak is an icon. It is the original luxury sports watch that created and defined the category. Introduced at BaselWorld in 1972 after being designed by Gérald Genta, it turned the Swiss industry upside down and changed the fortunes of the struggling Audemars Piguet. It’s no surprise, that Patek Philippe hired Gerald Genta a few years later to introduce their own version of a steel luxury sports watch: the Nautilus. This is a very special Audemars Piguet Royal Oak reference 15550SR.OO.1356SR.02. The case is two-tone in rose gold and stainless steel. It measures 37mm in diameter. It is powered by the calibre 5900. The bracelet will fit a wrist approximately 7 inches. The watch comes full set with box and papers. It comes from the original owner who cited he purchased the watch in 2024. These cards are not dated. The watch is running well and keeping good time.

title: Cartier Tank Louis Xl Jumbo 17002 in 18K White Gold Unpolished
description: The Cartier Tank Louis is one of the most sophisticated dress watches and these models have grown to become highly collectible over recent years. It is a great contrast to many sports Rolex models within a collection and can be worn in both a casual and dressed up state. This example dates to the 1970s. It features an 18K white gold case which is extremely rare. These are the largest vintage Cartier Tank models. The case measures 28mm in diameter and 35mm in length. It appears to be unpolished. The dial appears to be a service dial with SWISS at 6 o'clock. It is powered by the automatic calibre 170. This is an interesting model also worn by David Prowse (the famous actor who played Darth Vader in the Stars Wars Trilogy). Prowse owned a yellow gold example from the era. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well. It comes with a Cartier strap that is very short. It also comes with a white-gold Cartier deployant buckle.

title: Cartier Tortue Ref. 2496D with Service Papers + Receipt
description: This Cartier Tortue large reference 2496D is a great modern dress watch in 18k yellow gold. The Tortue case measures approximately 34mm at its widest point and 43mm lug-to-lug. The watch features a white guiloché dial with classic Roman numerals. The watch is paired with an 18k yellow gold deployant buckle and black crocodile strap. It features an exhibition caseback. The watch does not come with a box or papers. It was serviced by Cartier in 2025 and is running well.

title: A. Lange & Söhne Saxonia Outsize Date 381.031 in 18K RG Full Set
description: The case is made of 18K rose gold. The case measures 38.5mm in diameter. It is powered by the automatic calibre L086.8. It is paired on a A. Lange & Söhne strap with A. Lange & Söhne rose gold gold buckle. The watch was originally sold in 2021. The watch comes with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Jaeger-LeCoultre Memovox E 850 Unpolished
description: This is an uncommon Memovox model - a reference E 850. The cases on these are super cool and measure 33.5mm in diameter. These references were produced in the 50s and are incredibly rare. These were among the earliest water resistant Memovox models. They feature gorgeous dials with dagger markers. It is one of Charlie/s favorite Jaeger-LeCoultre references and he owns one in his personal collection that was given to him by Eric. To learn more about these special Memovox models, read Charlie Dunne’s Collectors Guide: The Jaeger-LeCoultre Memovox Reference E 850 . The watch does not include box and papers. The watch was just serviced and is running well.

title: Daniel Roth Ellipsocurvex Moon Phase Ref. 368.X.60 in 18K WG with Box
description: The Daniel Roth Ellipsocurvex is an incredible timepiece that was introduced in 1988. This watch dates to the mid-2000s. The case is 18k white gold. It measures approximately 38mm in diameter. It appears to be unpolished. This watch features an incredible guilloche dial with beautiful painted Roman numerals. The hand set on the Daniel Roth is very unique and attractive. The moonphase disc is stunning. The watch is paired on a Daniel Roth leather strap with white gold buckle. This is a great timepiece for those who appreciate refined independent watchmaking. The watch comes with box. It does not come with papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Abercrombie & Fitch Auto-Graph Unpolished
description: This Abercrombie & Fitch Auto-Mark is an uncommon and highly interesting model. The stainless steel case measures 35mm in diameter (approximately 42.5mm lug-to-lug). The case appears to be unpolished. It is paired on a contemporary beads of rice bracelet. The watch features a central hand that is changed through a pusher near 9 o’clock to mark a stopped time. The watch dates to the early 1950s. The watch does not come with a box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running great!

title: Abercrombie & Fitch Seafarer 2443 By Heuer Unpolished
description: The most desirable models from the retailer would be the Seafarer. The watch features a Valjoux 72 movement which was modified to incorporate a tide complication. The case appears to be unpolished. It measures in at 38mm wide. The watch is paired on a contemporary beads of rice bracelet. Learn more about these watches within Charlie Dunne’s article ‘ Collector's Guide: Vintage Abercrombie & Fitch Seafarer Watches ’. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Heuer Chronomatic Monaco Paintless Wonder Dial Reference 1133 Unpolished
description: The Heuer Monaco was introduced in 1969 with the first automatic chronograph movement, the calibre 11. Coupled by the association of Steve McQueen’s decision to wear the watch in the film ‘Le Mans’, the watch is nothing short of iconic. This example is one of the most famous Heuer Monacos on the planet (outside of the numerous Steve McQueen Le Mans models). It is one of the earliest examples known of the Heuer Monaco Chronomatic reference 1133. It is the rare variant with the “Chronomatic” font and luminous earlier hand set. The dial has developed an incredibly beautiful patina with the brass dial reacting through the blue paint - hence the nickname “Paintless Wonder” Monaco. The watch dates to circa 1969. The Heuer Monaco is actually quite a rare model and we are seeing more collectors recognize the reference 1133 as a staple within the vintage chronograph collection. This example is particularly special as it formerly belonged to the monumental vintage Heuer collector and historian, Jeff Stein. The watch was in Stein’s collection for over 18 years and was one of his most celebrated watches of all time. For those looking for one of the earliest examples of a historically important model, this is a grail watch. The case appears to be unpolished. It is stainless steel and measures approximately 38mm x 40mm. The watch does not come with a box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Tobey Steinman Heuer Carrera Reference 3647N Unpolished
description: This Heuer Carrera reference 3647N is an incredibly special example with the name Tobey Steinman printed at 6 o'clock. Tobey Steinman was a lady who was the chief buyer for Abercrombie & Fitch and lived in Ohio, where the company was headquartered. It is not clear what Ms. Steinman’s relationship with Heuer was, although perhaps she had been involved in the relationship between the manufacturer and Abercrombie & Fitch. leading to this incredibly rare personalized dial. The dial is a similar style as the iconic Heuer Carrera reference 3647 owned by James Garner which sold for $176,400 in 2022. This is one of only two black dial Heuer Carrera to have a name on it exclusively. We also sold the Sherman Decker Heuer Carrera reference 3647S , which was only the third example we have seen with a name on a Carrera. It features the the same font as the MG Carreras, but those were for MG customers and had the MG logo printed on the dial. The crystal had been removed from the watch for decades, leading to wear on the dial. This example dates to circa 1965-1966. We believe the case is unpolished with wear. It is powered by the Valjoux calibre 92. It is paired on a Gay Freres Bracelet for Heuer with HEL end links dating to 1965. You can read more about the origins of the Carrera in the in-depth article that I wrote back in 2013 . This is a very special Heuer Carrera and a rare opportunity to purchase a special piece of Heuer history. The watch does not come with box and papers. It was recently serviced and is running great.

title: Heuer Carrera Ref. 2447N Unpolished
description: The Carrera is an iconic sports chronograph which is one of the most versatile watches to have in a collection. This is a very attractive example with the black dial. The case appears to be unpolished. It measures 36 millimeters in diameter and 45mm lug-to-lug. The watch is powered by the Valjoux manual-winding calibre 72. It is paired on a aftermarket anonymous bracelet that looks great. The watch dates to the mid 1960s. It features the early hexagonal caseback. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running great.

title: Heuer “Gubelin” Autavia Ref. 2446 Unpolished
description: The Heuer Autavia is recognized by collectors as one of the great sports chronographs of the 1960s. Along with many of its contemporaries of the era, it is powered by the Valjoux 72. The reference 2446 is regarded as one of the great Heuer racing chronographs. The present example is extra special by the signed detail that features the retailer’s name “Gubelin”. The lugs feature a fluid design, tapering down toward the wrist with thinner, beveled lugs. The dimensions are 38mm in diameter with a height of 13mm. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch does not come with a box and papers. The service history is unknown, but it is running well.

title: Heuer Dato Carrera Reference 3147N Indianapolis Motor Speedway Indy 500
description: The Heuer Carrera is one of the legendary chronograph designs of the 20th century. Featuring stark angled lugs that were a product of the architecture of the 1960s, the present watch is notably a “first execution” and features an unpolished case. Finding Carreras from the 1960s with in great condition is extremely difficult. The reference 3147 was the first Heuer Carrera with date and this is a 3147N with the N meaning “Noir” indicating a black dial. The movement is a Landeron 189 with date and the case back is thicker on these to accommodate the thicker movement with the date. The case diameter is 36mm with a lug width of 18mm. The present example is a bit of a hodgepodge. The watch features service replacement hands with Super-LumiNova. The case has been lightly polished and it has a replacement crystal. The case back sticker is in tact. It is possible the dial was placed in the watch. Regardless, it is a very rare dial and highly coveted vintage Heuer. An Autavia model with this dial sold at Christie’s for nearly $200,000 back in 2017 . You can read more about the origins of the Carrera in the in-depth article that I wrote for HODINKEE back in 2013 . We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers.

title: Heuer Dato Carrera Ref. 3147S Indianapolis Motor Speedway Indy 500 Unpolished
description: The Heuer Carrera is one of the legendary chronograph designs of the 20th century. Featuring stark angled lugs that were a product of the architecture of the 1960s, the present watch is notably a “first execution”. Finding Carreras from the 1960s in great condition is extremely difficult. The reference 3147 was the first Heuer Carrera with date and this is a 3147S with the S meaning “Silver” indicating a black dial. The movement is a Landeron 148 with date and the case back is thicker on these to accommodate the thicker movement with the date. The case appears to be unpolished. The diameter measures approximately 36mm with a lug width of 18mm. We are not sure of the provenance of the watch, but it is an unbelievably attractive example. This is a grail watch and perhaps a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for Heuer and racing enthusiasts. This example features the Indianapolis Motor Speedway logo and an Autavia model with this dial sold at Christie’s for nearly $200,000 back in 2017 . You can read more about the origins of the Carrera in the in-depth article that I wrote for HODINKEE back in 2013 . It was just serviced and is running well. It does not come with a box or papers.

title: Universal Geneve Space-Compax Reference 885104 on Leather
description: The Universal Geneve Space-Compax was designed by the company to be their underwater dive chronograph. Not many were produced at the time and very few survive in excellent condition today. The case has been polished in the past.This watch is from the late 1960s. It is powered by the manual-wind movement (Caliber 72 made by Valjoux), and is 40mm in diameter. It does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Universal Genève Eric Clapton Tri-Compax Reference 881101/01
description: This Universal Genève Tri-Compax reference 881101/01 is a very special and rare complicated UG. Eric Clapton wore a similar model when he was part of Cream and the watch now has the moniker “Eric Clapton” in the watch community. It has a 2.43 million serial number. The case has been lightly polished. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Universal Geneve Compax Ref. 885103 w/ Evil Nina Dial
description: This is a Universal Geneve Compax reference 885103. It features an Evil Nina dial. We have no reason to believe the dial is not original to the watch, but the serial is not visible. The case has been lightly polished in the past. It features a replacement crown. For those looking for a great deal on a vintage UG, this is a sick watch. It has a manual-wind movement (Caliber 72 made by Valjoux), and measures 36mm in diameter, and approximately 45mm lug-to-lug. It does not include the original box or papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Universal Genève Dato-Compax Reference 22325 W/ WWII Provenance Unpolished
description: This is more than just a spectacular Universal Geneve Dato-Compax chronograph. It was Mayhew Y. "Bo" Foster's timekeeper on May 9, 1945 while he flew Hermann Göring in a Stinson L-5 Sentinel from Kitzbuhel, Austria to Augsburg, Germany for interrogation by the 7th Army before he later stood trial at Nuremberg. “Bo" Foster (October 9, 1911 – March 21, 2011) was a decorated American pilot and hero. Foster graduated in 1937 with a degree in English from Yale. For his actions in World War II - including 70 reconnaissance combat missions - Foster was awarded the Silver Star for his service in France in 1944, the Air Medal, and the Légion d'Honneur for his contribution to liberating France. Foster later reached the rank of Brigadier General in the Montana Army National Guard Foster transported Göring in the L-5, a larger plane than the L-4 he normally piloted, because Göring weighed more than 300 pounds. In a letter to his wife, Virginia, written at the time, Foster described his first impression of Göring as "effeminate [and he] gave me the creeps . . . Several times I had the impulse to turn the plane over and see if I could shake him out, but he was wedged in like a champagne cork… He acted as though he was going on a sightseeing tour, or really as though I was going on a sightseeing tour, and he was showing me where he grew up. I had a .45 in a shoulder holster, but he couldn't reach that. But neither could I, because I had two hands controlling the plane.” When Foster arrived, there was just a single jeep at the airstrip to meet the arriving flight. Foster rode with Göring and formally turned him over to the intelligence officer without ceremony. It seems likely that Göring was also wearing a Universal Geneve chronograph in steel on that flight - in his case an oversized non-luminous Compax reference 22430 that was in his possession at Nuremberg and sold at auction in 2016. Göring was eventually convicted of war crimes, but took a smuggled cyanide pill on October 15,

title: Ulysse Nardin Chronograph Ref. 7536-2 Unpolished
description: This Ulysse Nardin chronograph reference 7536-2 is one of the best models from Ulysse Nardin. These are extremely cool and uncommon chronographs. These watches are massive 38mm chronographs. The lugs are extremely attractive and feature the beveled edges. The case appears to be unpolished. It is powered by the Valjoux 72 movement. It features an attractive matte black dial with the applied anchor logo. The dot over 90 bezel is strong and does not have cracks. These are quite cool as they feature nice grooves throughout the bezel. These have sold as high as $72,000 at auction . For those who have a penchant for interesting alternative chronographs, this is a great watch. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers.

title: Ulysse Nardin Blast Tourbillon Reference 1723-400/03 Full Set
description: This Ulysse Nardin Blast Tourbillon is an awesome wristwatch. It is powered by the skeletonized self-winding tourbillon calibre UN-172. Ulysse Nardin is known for their daring designs, and this model is certainly one that collectors love. The reference 1723-400 was introduced in 2020 as the first skeletonized automatic tourbillon from Ulysse Nardin. It is a highly innovative model. It measures 45mm in diameter but wears very nice on the wrist. The case is made of titanium and is quite comfortable. The watch dates to 2020 We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does comes with box and papers. It comes from a collector who is a boss. GOOD PROVENANCE!

title: Breguet Tradition Seconde Rétrograde 7037BB/11/9V6 w/ Papers Unpolished
description: The Breguet Tradition 7037BB is an incredible design that has been highly appreciated from the prestigious watchmaker. The 18k white gold case measures 39mm in diameter (46mm lug-to-lug). Like within the vintage Breguet models, it has an awesome coin edge profile and fantastic buckle design. The watch is powered by the automatic calibre 505SR. The watch is a beautiful timepiece with the retrograde seconds hand. This watch comes with a service pouch and Certificate of Origin. We do not know the service history but it is running well. We do not know the date of production.

title: Vulcain Cricket OG Model with Arabic Numeral Dial Variant Unpolished
description: This Vulcain Cricket is is an amazing example produced in La-Chaux-de-Fonds. It measures 34mm in diameter (just under 43mm lug-to-lug). The case is unpolished. The watch is paired on a period correct stretch rivet bracelet made by Gay Freres. The dial is an incredibly nice LBJ variant which was the style worn by Lyndon Baines Johnson while he served as Senator of Texas. The watch is powered by the calibre 120. This is one of the most attractive Vulcain Crickets to own! The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Vulcain Cricket Black Dial Reference S2328A Unpolished
description: A Unpolished This Vulcain Cricket reference S2328A is a fantastic and rare example with the rare black dial. These are incredibly rare and attractive models. It is powered by the calibre MSR S2. The case is unpolished. It features the very cool “Officer” style lugs, and an angled bezel. The case measures 35mm in diameter (41.5mm lug-to-lug). The alarm is very loud and will surely wake you up when it rings! The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Vulcain Cricket Grey Dial Ref S2328A Unpolished
description: A Unpolished This Vulcain Cricket reference S2328A is a fantastic and rare example with the rare grey metallic dial with a mirror track. Over the years of collecting, I have only seen three examples - one of which is in Eric’s personal collection which he wore in the Rolex Explorer Reference Points video! The watch has a blue “RA” stamp on the outside of “Swiss Made” at 6 o’clock. It is powered by the calibre MSR S2. The case is unpolished. It features the very cool “Officer” style lugs, and an angled bezel. The case measures 35mm in diameter (41.5mm lug-to-lug). The alarm is very loud and will surely wake you up when it rings! The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: OMEGA Speedmaster Professional Reference 105.012-66 CB Case Unpolished
description: A Speedmaster Professional Reference 105.012-66 CB Case Unpolished The OMEGA Speedmaster was introduced in 1957, initially created for drivers in automotive racing. However, it would reach iconic status by eventually reaching spaceflight qualification by NASA amongst several of the highest grade chronographs of its era. This is a nice OMEGA Speedmaster reference 105.012. The reference 105.012 was the first Speedmaster with crown and pusher guards, garnering the “Professional” name on the dial for the case upgrade. It features a stepped dial, and an applied OMEGA logo. This is a very special OMEGA Speedmaster 105.012-66. The watch comes from the family of the original owner. Eric purchased it for his personal collection in 2021. It is powered by the highly admired calibre 321, which was recently re-released to the excitement of many Speedy lovers. The reference 105.012 was the first asymmetrical case to be released in the Speedmaster line from 1963 to 1966. The case was made by CB (le Centrale Boites). The case appears to be unpolished. The dimensions are 42mm in diameter with a lug width of 20mm. It is paired on a OMEGA 1116 bracelet with 575 end links which is original to the watch. The bracelet will fit a wrist over 7 inches. To learn more about the OMEGA Speedmaster, you can watch my ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Entire Lineage Of The OMEGA Speedmaster ’ video and read the corresponding article. The watch does not come with box and papers. It was issued an Extract from the Archives, but we cannot locate the physical Extract. We have attached a photo below. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: OMEGA Speedmaster Racing Dial Ref. 145.022-69 ST Full Set w/ Extract
description: A Speedmaster Racing Dial Ref. 145.022-69 ST Full Set w/ Extract The OMEGA Speedmaster is certainly one of the most iconic watches with a truly rich history of exploration and sport. This is an incredible “Racing Dial” reference 145.022-69. The watch was originally delivered to Japan in 1971 and was sold in 1975 according to the papers. The racing dial is one of the most exciting and interesting dial variants on any Speedy. These models are very rare and this example is in awesome condition. The dial is incredibly attractive. The case has been lightly polished. It comes with a contemporary OMEGA bracelet and is paired on an OMEGA 1039 bracelet dating to 1970. It is powered by the calibre 861 manual wind movement. This example is a very special watch that was sold at Phillips' START-STOP-RESET: 88 Epic Stainless Steel Chronographs . The watch comes as a full set with a box and papers. It comes with the Extract from the Archives. It also comes with the leather bound book of START-STOP-RESET: 88 Epic Stainless Steel Chronographs. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. To learn more about the Omega Speedmaster, you can read my ‘ Reference Points: Understanding The Omega Speedmaster ’ article and corresponding video with HODINKEE.

title: OMEGA Speedmaster Reduced Blue Kart Ref. 175.0032 / PIC 3810.80.08 From Paul Newman & Carl Haas Full Set + Extract
description: A Speedmaster Reduced Blue Kart Ref. 175.0032 / PIC 3810.80.08 From Paul Newman & Carl Haas Full Set + Extract The OMEGA Speedmaster is certainly one of the most iconic watches with a truly rich history of exploration and sport. This is a particularly cool limited edition watch with incredible provenance. It is an OMEGA Speedmaster Reduced Blue Kart Edition reference 3510.81 that was gifted by Paul Newman and Carl Haas to the Newman/Haas Racing team’s body engineer Bill Mann during Christmas of 1997. The watch was featured in HODINKEE’s article ‘ Found An Omega Speedmaster Gifted By Paul Newman ’ in 2016. It was later sold at Heritage Auctions in 2019. The case is unpolished. It measures 39mm in diameter. This watch comes with box and papers. It also comes with an Extract from the Archives. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. The box is designed like a racing tire which is insanely cool. The watch dates to 1997. To learn more about the OMEGA Speedmaster, you can read my ‘ Reference Points: Understanding The OMEGA Speedmaster ’ article and corresponding video with HODINKEE.

title: OMEGA Speedmaster “Ed White” 105.003-65 Full Set and Extract Unpolished
description: A Speedmaster “Ed White” 105.003-65 Full Set and Extract Unpolished It is no secret that I love vintage OMEGA Speedmasters. You can see the HODINKEE Reference Points video I did on the subject with Ben Clymer. This is an incredible reference 105.003, also referred to as the “Ed White” as it was famously worn by the iconic NASA astronaut. The watch dates to circa 1966. It is powered by the iconic calibre 321, which was recently re-released and garnered great reception and excitement from a large portion of watch collectors. The case appears to be unpolished. The dimensions are 38.5mm in diameter (or 48mm lug-to-lug) with a lug width of 19mm. The dial is gorgeous and features tritium lume that has patinated with age. It is paired with an Omega 7912 bracelet dating to 1966. To learn more about the Omega Speedmaster, you can watch ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Entire Lineage Of The Omega Speedmaster ’ video I made with Ben Clymer in 2015 (and corresponding article ). The watch comes full set with box, papers and with an additional receipt. The watch was sold in 1967 in the United Kingdom. It comes with an Extract from the Archives. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: OMEGA Speedmaster Reference 145.022-69 BA In 18K YG
description: A Speedmaster Reference 145.022-69 BA in 18K YG OMEGA introduced the Speedmaster in 1957, initially created for drivers in automotive racing needing to time their laps. However, the Speedmaster would reach eternal iconic status by eventually being qualified for spaceflight by NASA after an intense testing of several of the highest-grade chronographs of the 1960s. NASA selected the Speedmaster as the exclusive watch for use by its astronauts. The OMEGA Speedmaster reference 145.022-69 BA was the first OMEGA Speedmaster to be produced in 18k yellow gold. Only 30 examples were produced in total for astronauts and two were produced for President Nixon and Vice President Agnew. The next examples were given to Astronauts and are considered by many to be the grail OMEGA Speedmasters. On October 20, 2022, Wally Schirra’s personal OMEGA Speedmaster Professional BA 145.022 was sold for $1,906,954 . This example is one that was sold to the public. The 18K yellow-gold case is in has been lightly polshed. The dial is fantastic and the bezel remains in good condition. The watch is powered by the caliber 861. The bracelet is long and should fit a wrist approximately 7.1 inches. Finding an example with a long bracelet is incredibly difficult. For those looking for an epic gold Speedmaster, these are amazing watches. To learn more about the OMEGA Speedmaster, you can watch my ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Entire Lineage Of The OMEGA Speedmaster ’ video and read the corresponding article. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do now know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Roger Dubuis Hommage Chronograph Reference H37 in 18K White Gold Full Set
description: This Roger Dubuis Hommage Chronograph reference H37 is an incredibly sophisticated timepiece. The dial features luminous numerals and demarcations within the multi-tone sector dial. It features an attractive cream colored dial with luminous feuille (leaf) hands. These dial layouts are extremely attractive and pay homage to the iconic chronographs of the 1930s. The case is made of 18k white gold and measures approximately 37mm in diameter. The watch is powered by the calibre RD56. The watch features an exhibition caseback displaying the manual wind movement. These movements were chronometer certified and it accompanies the original papers when tested in 2000. It is paired with an aftermarket leather strap and buckle. This watch comes with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Zenith El Primero Reference A386 Unpolished on Gay Frères Bracelet
description: Introduced in 1969, the Zenith El Primero Reference A386 sits amongst the most celebrated chronographs in watchmaking. Powered by the automatic high-beat calibre 3019. The model’s hands and hour markers feature a pale yellow tritium that immediately catches the attention of the wearer. Competing with the tri-colored subdials, the attributes of this watch are really a beautiful testament to the sports watches of yesteryear. The watch is 38mm wide (with a lug-to-lug length of 45.5mm). The lug width is 19mm and the height is 12.5mm including the crystal. The case appears to be unpolished. It is paired on a the rare and incredibly cool Zenith ladder Gay Frères bracelet dating to circa 1971. The bracelet will fit a wrist approximately 7.5 inches. We do not know the service history, but it is running great. It does not come with box or papers.

title: Zenith El Primero Ref A386 on Gay Freres Bracelet Unpolished
description: Introduced in 1969, the Zenith El Primero Reference A386 sits amongst the most celebrated chronographs in watchmaking. This particular example comes with the Gay Frères steel ladder bracelet dating to 1969. The watch is 38mm wide (with a lug-to-lug length of 45.5mm). title: Titus Big Crown Calypsomatic Ref. 7840 Unpolished
description: This Titus Calypsomatic reference 7840 is an extremely cool vintage dive watch. It is reminiscent of many Rolex Big Crown Submariners and there is a strong collector community for these watches. The watch features the nicest and most attractive glossy dial I have seen on any example. It features warm patina on the hands and markers - which are tritium. This is like wearing a Big Crown without radium! The stainless steel case measures approximately 38mm in diameter (48mm lug-to-lug). The watch comes with an original three link bracelet signed by Titus. For those looking for a world class Titus Big Crown Calypsomatic, this is one of the best! The watch does not come with a box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Longines Legend Diver w/ JB Champion Stretch Bracelet Unpolished w/ Box & Papers
description: This Longines Legend Diver is an incredible vintage dive watch in fantastic condition. The watch measures 42mm in diameter, and approximately 53mm lug-to-lug. It features a stunning black dial that has begun to turn tropical. It comes with a stretch bracelet made by JB Champion. It features a beautiful gilt tropical dial. The comes with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Longines 13ZN Chronograph Reference 5415 w/ Extract
description: This Longines reference 5415 is a special vintage chronograph with the rare snapback waterproof compressor case. The watch features the legendary calibre 13ZN which was used from circa 1936-1947 within Longines chronographs. The calibre 13ZN is considered one of the most important chronograph movements and is cherished by collectors. This example was invoiced to Longines-Wittnauer Watch Co in the United States on October 27, 1947. The case measures 37.5mm in diameter. The case has been lightly polished. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers. It comes with an Extract from the Archives.

title: Longines Greenlander Reference 5707 w/ Extract Unpolished
description: The Longines reference 5707 is a special watch known as the “Greenlander” is an important military Longines and one of the most desired and rarer models from the Dirty Dozen wristwatches. The stainless steel case measures 37.5mm in diameter by 48mm lug to lug. This watch was produced in 1945 according to the Extract from the Archives and was invoiced to Baume & Co. of the United Kingdom. This is a special example with the matching number stamped on the bottom of the of the lug which coincides with the case back number. The case appears to be unpolished. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers. It comes with an Extract from the Archives. For those looking for a special military Longines, these are incredible watches.

title: Longines Swissair 24-Hour Reference 6630 w/ Extract from the Archives
description: This Longines is an incredibly interesitng and rare oversized wristwatch made for Swissair pilots. The stainless steel case is a massive 47mm in diameter and 57mm lug-to-lug. The watch displays a 24-hour dial. It features a spade hour hand and leaf minute hand. The watch features a 9mm onion crown. The watch was invoiced to Swissair in 1957. These watches have sold as high as $176,000 at auction. For those looking for incredible aviation Longines timepieces, these are special watches. The watch does not come with a box or papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well. It comes with Extract from the Archives. The watch is paired on the original strap and buckle appears to be original.

title: Enicar Sherpa Reference 140/013 Unpolished
description: This Enicar Sherpa is an exceptionally cool stainless steel wristwatch. The case measures approximately 35mm in diameter and just over 42mm lug-to-lug. The watch features a sunburst soleil dial that has turned to a warm silver hue. The dial has printed numerals at the 6, 9 and 12 positions and features a date window at 3 o’clock on the dial. This watch is from circa 1964, does not include box or papers, has a manual-wind movement (Caliber AR 1141). We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Enicar Mk 3 Sherpa Graph Reference 072-02-01 Unpolished
description: The Enicar Sherpa Graph models are extremely desirable for collectors and very difficult to find. The present watch is a fantastic example with the case made by E. Piquerez SA (also called EPSA). Enicar was way ahead of other companies with the white registers against a dark blue dial and a large 40mm diameter case with a tachymeter scale. The case appears to be unpolished. It is a “Mark III” / “Mark 3” model with reference 072-02-01 on the case back. It features the original signed Compressor crown with the Saturn logo, while the earliest examples have no logo. If you are looking for a large alternative cool sports chronograph , this is really is such a watch! It is paired on an Enicar bracelet that was later added. This watch does not include box or papers, has a manual-wind movement (Caliber 72 made by Valjoux), and is 40mm in diameter. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Enicar Seapearl Ref. 124/003 Unpolished

title: Rolex Tiffany & Co. Great White Sea-Dweller Reference 1665
description: This Rolex “Great White” Sea-Dweller reference 1665 is an incredibly special watch featuring a Tiffany & Co. signed dial. . The dial features a beautiful yellow lume. It is a “Maxi” Sea-Dweller dial and was among the last examples of the legendary reference 1665 made. These examples with 6 million serial numbers have the extremely large hour markers that give them the “Maxi” moniker. I find them to be the most beautiful Great White Sea-Dweller dials. The reference 1665 models with all-white text are known as “Great White” models and the early examples are known as “Double Red” Sea-Dwellers with two red lines of text and the earliest, essentially prototype and not-for-sale, Sea-Dwellers are known as “Single Red” Sea-Dwellers with a single line of red text. The case has been polished in the past. It features a 6.7M serial dating to circa 1981. The lug-to-lug length is 47mm and it measures 40mm in diameter excluding the crown. It is paired on a later service Rolex 93150 Oyster bracelet from circa 1991 and later 501B end links. The watch does not come box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well. The watch recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar. It features a TrueDome D39 crystal.

title: Urwerk UR-106 ‘Only Watch’ Full Set Mint Condition
description: This Urwerk reference UR-106 was made as a Piece Unique for Only Watch. The watch features an aggressive case shape which is crafted from titanium with a black PVD coating. The dimensions measure approximately 50 x 35mm. The watch features satellite hours indication which gives the appearance of analog and digital time. It is powered by the automatic calibre UR-6.01. For those looking for something eclectic, and highly interesting this is a great opportunity. Despite our passion leaning towards vintage watches, there are certainly a number of modern watches that are undeniably awesome. Urwerk watches represent forward thinking watchmaking and get just about everyone excited - whether you are simply curious about watches or are amazed at the linear format on the timepiece. This is truly a fun watch to wear. The watch comes with box and papers. We do not know the service history of the watch but it is running well. It was previously sold at Phillips for the 2015 “Only Watch” charity auction in favour of research on Duchenne muscular dystrophy, and belonged to an incredible collector! It comes with the 2 year International Warranty paperwork from Urwerk dating to 2020.

description: The Rolex-Domino’s connection is perhaps the ultimate high-low collaboration. These watches were not made for purchase by the public, but as a way to reward Domino’s franchise owners who hit their sales targets. All these watches were originally ordered through Schlanderer and Sons in Ann Arbor, Michigan, where Domino’s has its headquarters. In the past, these watches on the secondhand market were generally the least expensive Rolex a person could purchase as few people wanted a pizza logo like this on their dial. Dealers would buy them, swap out the Domino’s dial, and polish off the case back initials. Over the last year, however, they have gained a massive following. The watch features an engraving on the back with the recipient’s initials. You can learn about these watches in our video Collector Conversation: Tom Monaghan - Founder of Domino's Pizza - on the Domino's Rolex . This version features the “tilted logo” that is the last version of Dominos’s Rolex watch with the logo on the dial. . The watch features a U^ serial dating to 1997. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch comes as a “full set” with a box, papers and hangtag. It was originally sold in 1998. We do not know the full service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar. To learn more about Rolex-Domino’s story, watch the video ”Rolex Model NEVER in Stores” . title: Audemars Piguet Tropical Royal Oak A Series Reference 5402ST
description: A Series Reference 5402ST The Audemars Piguet Royal Oak is an icon. It is the original luxury sports watch that created and defined the category. Introduced at BaselWorld in 1972 after being designed by Gérald Genta, it turned the Swiss industry upside down and changed the fortunes of the struggling Audemars Piguet. It’s no surprise, that Patek Philippe hired Gerald Genta a few years later to introduce their own version of a steel luxury sports watch: the Nautilus. The origin of the species is the Royal Oak reference 5402ST - nicknamed the “Jumbo”. It is no surprise that the A series examples are hotly hunted and desired by collectors around the world. Only a few seem come to market each year - at most. I am thrilled and honored to offer this incredible example with a beautiful tropical dial. Often these early dials can have an uneven and sometimes unattractive patina, whereas this dial is a gorgeous and even example. The watch should fit a wrist up slightly over 7 inches and features the original flip “Audemars Piguet” flip clasp (often replaced with the AP flip clasp) with the Gay Freres “GF” logo. The watch dates to circa 1972. The case measures 39mm in diameter (48mm lug to lug) and this is the original “Jumbo”. The case and bracelet have been lightly polished in the past like on the vast majority of these, but this case is still super attractive on the wrist. This watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. For those hunting for an incredible A Series Royal Oak, do not sleep on this watch!

The case appears to be unpolished. Overall this is an outstanding example. The watch is powered by the calibre 825, the first automatic alarm wristwatch to incorporate the calendar complication. The movement is a bumper-automatic, which means it does not rotate a full 360 degrees. Instead, the oscillating weight will bounce back and forth between two spring sides within the movement. Along with the Atmos clock and Reversos, Jaeger-LeCoultre’s advancements in alarm timepieces throughout the 20th century are certainly one of the most iconic genres from the Le Sentier manufacturer. Perhaps the quintessential Memovox is the reference E 855 from the 1960s. The reference’s “E” stands for Etanche, which indicates the case is a water-resistant model. It does not come with box and papers. The watch was recently serviced and is running well.
